# Episode 002 approved introduction (verbatim, do not edit)

Preserved exactly as approved on 2026-10-08. SCRIPT.md uses this text unchanged in sections 01 and 02.

---

If you've been following Marvel comics for the last decade or so, you've probably heard the name Jonathan Hickman.

Fantastic Four. Avengers. Secret Wars. House of X. Powers of X.

This guy has written some of the biggest, most ambitious stories Marvel has published in recent memory. And with the MCU exploring so many of the same enormous concepts, it's not surprising that people are paying attention to his work.

But here's something funny.

I've been collecting comics for most of my life. And for years, I was picking up these strange books called East of West and The Manhattan Projects.

I loved the covers. They were sparse, mysterious, sometimes almost completely devoid of the usual comic-book clutter. And the artwork inside? Especially in The Manhattan Projects? Just completely nuts. It had this weird, almost Garbage Pail Kids quality that I absolutely loved.

And somehow, until pretty recently, I hadn't connected those books with Jonathan Hickman.

So that got me thinking.

A lot of people know Hickman because of Marvel. But how many have explored the bizarre, inventive comics he was making outside of it?

Because if you like what he did with the X-Men, or the enormous interconnected story that led to Secret Wars, there's a whole other side of his work worth discovering.

And that's what I want to talk about today.
